tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description opens with imperative phrasing ('Use this skill whenever a user asks about...') and explicitly lists a large set of trigger contexts (slow ONTAP, SSD full, SnapMirror lag, NFS/SMB/AD failures, stuck states, backup/snapshot/failover, sizing, CLI requests, change requests) framed around user-reported symptoms and needs rather than internal implementation. It also explicitly carves out an exclusion case (best-practices/pillar audits) and a negative scope (not for FSx Windows/Lustre/OpenZFS/EFS), which is pushy and thorough. While dense, it is a single sentence/field intended for machine matching, and remains focused on when to use the skill rather than how it works internally.
tests.evidence: "Use this skill whenever a user asks about an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system (any type, or named only as SVM/aggregate), EXCEPT best-practices/pillar or pass/fail posture audits (never load for those). Use for: slow ONTAP; SSD full; throughput/IOPS/burst limits; tiering; SnapMirror lag; NFS/SMB/AD failures..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but almost entirely domain-specific: it describes exact API calls, field names, thresholds, and non-obvious ONTAP/FSx behaviors the agent would not otherwise know. There is minimal explanation of generic concepts like what a file system or NFS is.
tests.evidence: "Never ask for a fact the AWS API can enumerate... Ask only for what no API returns: client-side command and error text, client IP..."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (thresholds, metric catalogs, CLI command packs, severity bands) are consistently pushed into references/ files rather than embedded in the body, even within conditional routing tables.
tests.evidence: "Thresholds and severity bands live there — don't paraphrase them from memory." and the routing table links out to REFERENCE.md sections rather than inlining content.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ (REFERENCE.md, cloudtrail-audit.md, cloudwatch-metrics.md, dependencies-and-errors.md, deployment-types.md, ontap-cli-pack.md, review-checks.md, unlisted-symptoms.md) is linked via markdown links in the body.
tests.evidence: "[REFERENCE.md](references/REFERENCE.md) — failure-mode playbook §1–§11..." and similar links for all other reference files in the References section and inline.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: References specify precise conditions for loading, e.g. tied to deployment type lookup, specific symptom routing table, or specific item lookups.
tests.evidence: "read [deployment-types.md](references/deployment-types.md)" immediately after "before quoting any ceiling, threshold, or metric dimension" — and the routing table maps specific symptoms to specific reference files.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (write boundary, backup deletion, CLI pack delivery) are highly prescriptive with exact wording and sequencing, while analytical judgment areas (severity assignment, inference labeling) are described with reasoning/purpose rather than rigid scripts.
tests.evidence: "A closing that works: 'Those are configuration changes you'd want to make deliberately rather than something I'd do silently.'" alongside flexible guidance like "Separate observed from inferred... marked 'consistent with…' plus the evidence that would confirm it."

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple options could apply (e.g., tool calls, metric sources), the skill designates specific defaults/order rather than listing equal alternatives; no clear case of an un-prioritized tool menu was found.
tests.evidence: "Capacity questions — run these in order and name each: 1. cloudwatch:ListMetrics... 2. SSD totals... 3. Per volume..."

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable diagnostic approach (identify target, collect data, run checks, produce remediation, report, validate) applicable to any FSx ONTAP file system, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: "Track progress through these steps. Every run completes Steps 1–3 and 6..." followed by generic Step 1–6 workflow applicable to any file system.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: Gotchas-like content is woven throughout (false-signal suppression, EC2 CPU~100% by design, tiering cooling period, shared metric names with Windows) rather than in a separate section, but it is present and concrete.
tests.evidence: "e.g. EC2-level CPU ~100% is by design; tiering that hasn't moved data inside its cooling period is by design"

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill explicitly defines a structured report template with required sections.
tests.evidence: "Produce a Markdown report named fsx-ontap-review-<fsid>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md... Summary — ... Findings — table... Change history — ... Recommendations — ... Data gaps — ... Escalation-readiness packet — ... Appendix — ..."

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The report template outline in Step 5 is a short bullet-point skeleton well under 20 lines, not a large inline template.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The only asset file, sample-fsx-context.json, is explicitly linked in the body.
tests.evidence: "If no live access is available, use [sample-fsx-context.json](assets/sample-fsx-context.json) as the working context so the review can still be demonstrated end to end."

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset link clearly specifies the condition for use (no live access available).
tests.evidence: "If no live access is available, use [sample-fsx-context.json](assets/sample-fsx-context.json) as the working context..."

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from the skill root with no traversal or absolute path.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The procedural workflow is presented as a checkbox checklist with Step N format, and subsequent detailed sections use matching '## Step N:' headings.
tests.evidence: "- [ ] Step 1: Identify the target file system and gather symptoms" ... followed by "## Step 1: Identify the target file system and gather symptoms" matching headings for Steps 2-6.

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: Step 6 is an explicit self-validation checklist the agent runs against its own draft before presenting the final report.
tests.evidence: "## Step 6: Validate the reply before presenting it\n\nCheck your own draft against this list and fix anything that fails before sending:"
